$comment: Field-building work, as a third domain alongside technical and policy.
WHY THIS EXISTS. The first cut tagged every role at a field-building organization as
'open to any agenda'. That produced 81 such roles, but only 10 were actually cohort
programmes where a mentor determines placement. The other 71 were ordinary jobs: an
operations manager at Constellation, a software engineer at Lightcone, a grants associate
at Coefficient Giving. Calling those 'open to any agenda' was wrong twice over: it hid real
jobs behind a non-answer, and it diluted the label so that the genuine fellowships stopped
So field-building gets its own categories, roles at those orgs inherit normally, and
'open to any agenda' is reserved for Fellowship / Internship / Course positions, where it
is a true statement about how placement works rather than an admission that we did not tag.
DOMAIN 'meta' IS NOT MATCHED. The matcher handles technical and policy only. That is
deliberate: these categories are close to worldview-neutral, someone who wants to run a
fellowship programme is not thereby committed to a position on scheming, so ranking them
against an instrument result would be inventing a signal. They appear in browse and on the
agendas page, and they carry no coordinates.

agendas.name: Talent pipelines and training
agendas.one_sentence_summary: Find people who could do this work, and get them to the point where they can.
agendas.theory_of_change: The field's binding constraint is often people rather than money → structured training, mentorship and placement convert interested outsiders into productive researchers and policy staff faster than they would convert on their own → the pipeline that fills every other agenda on this page.
agendas.why_it_is_not_matched: Worldview-neutral by construction: the programmes place people across every agenda, so a position on the axes would misrepresent them.

agendas.name: Grantmaking and funding infrastructure
agendas.one_sentence_summary: Decide where the money goes, and build the machinery that moves it.
agendas.theory_of_change: Most safety work is grant-funded and the funding is highly concentrated → the quality of grantmaking judgement is a large multiplier on the whole field → adding capacity and independent judgement here moves more than adding one more researcher.
agendas.why_it_is_not_matched: A grantmaker's job is to fund across worldviews, not to hold one.

agendas.name: Community, tooling and research infrastructure
agendas.one_sentence_summary: Build and run the things the rest of the field depends on but nobody is individually paid to maintain.
agendas.theory_of_change: Forums, venues, datasets, job boards and shared tooling are public goods with no natural owner → someone maintaining them well raises the productivity of everyone using them → chronically under-supplied relative to their leverage.
agendas.why_it_is_not_matched: Infrastructure serves every agenda; positioning it on the axes would be a category error.
